record.question: Sacrificial rites performed for good crops is
record.explanation: Hnuaipui is the Mizo crop/harvest sacrifice - 'hnua' denotes the standing paddy crop, and other MPSC papers in the same corpus describe 'hnuaipui' as the sacrifice in which a full-grown pig is killed and as the offering made to the god of sun and rain. The alternatives do not fit: Chung is the memorial feast for the dead, Fano Dawi is the post-harvest/new-year festival (not a sacrificial rite), and Hnuaite is the offering made to the guardian spirit Lasi.
